newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn's Kinkel urges Britain to set pro-EU course.
newsitem.headline: Bonn's Kinkel urges Britain to set pro-EU course.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel has urged fellow EU-member Britain, in unusually emphatic terms, to commit itself to a future in the European Union.
"A general election will be held in Britain no later than May," Kinkel said in a New Year statement released on Sunday.
"The country must reach a clear decision on its European policy. Britain belongs to Europe. Europe needs Britain."
The comments came at the top of a list of important events likely to shape German foreign policy in 1997.

Kinkel went on to renew earlier affirmations that the planned single currency -- one of the most controversial aspects of EU membership for Britain -- would happen and that preparations would continue through 1997.

He also called for renewed efforts to ensure the success of efforts currently in progress to streamline EU decision-making and reduce individual countries' veto powers -- another source of irritation to British euro-sceptics.

"In the EU we need decision-making by majority, effective organisational structures, a foreign and security policy expressed with one voice, and progress in home and legal affairs which citizens can identify with," Kinkel said.
